definitions: A cyberattack that exploits a previously unknown vulnerability in a computer system or software, for which no patch or fix has been released.
An attack that occurs on or before the day a software vulnerability becomes publicly known, giving developers zero days to create a defense.
examples: The company was hit by a sophisticated zero-day attack.
Security experts are constantly on the lookout for new zero-day attack vectors.
A successful zero-day attack can have devastating consequences.
